located within the Los Angeles, California fashion district (referred to hereafter as the
“Los Angeles Fashion District GTO”).12 The Los Angeles Fashion District GTO applied
to certain specified types of “Covered Businesses,” including “perfume stores,” in a
“Covered Geographic Area” that encompassed A&S’s Fine Fragrance location at 501
East Olympic Boulevard.13

course of its trade or business, received currency in excess of $3,000 in one transaction
or two or more related transactions in a 24-hour period, to report such transactions
electronically to FinCEN.14 The Los Angeles Fashion District GTO was effective from
October 9, 2014 through April 6, 2015.

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: Insufficient facts to determine whether 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring here.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring (and related conduct) done “for the purpose of evading” Bank Secrecy Act reporting requirements (e.g., causing or attempting to cause a domestic financial institution to fail to file a required report such as a CTR, or structuring transactions to evade such reporting). The fact pattern shows multiple cash ATM withdrawals (roughly $282–$759 each) and two wires ($5,581.46 and $3,365.26), none of which are near the typical $10,000 CTR threshold and there is no indication of cash deposits, currency exchanges, or other reportable currency transactions being broken up to avoid reporting. Critically, § 5324 requires an evasion purpose/intent; the facts provide no evidence of intent to evade reporting (no statements, patterns of just-under-threshold cash deposits, or bank reporting interactions). Therefore, based on the provided transactions alone, it cannot be determined whether the conduct falls within § 5324.
